scope: All 30 residual candidates: 10 each ha/ig/ln; direct target-language grammar and UI semantics review. No recredit of the other 331 rows per language.

context.main: The authoritative catalogue has ui_main23=Main immediately before ui_drawing23=Drawing and ui_colour_tab23=Color. Review as a generic main/primary heading only; no exact current consumer or specific palette-section identity is established. This does not change the separate palette-action composition assessment.
context.palette_argument_3: Localized imperative action to expand/collapse the palette, supported by the existing Expand colour palette / Collapse colour palette catalogue. Acceptance evaluates that meaningful action reading. Do not supply an English action, a full duplicated palette sentence, or an adjective/palette name; such substitutions have a different grammar. Runtime wiring is not certified.
context.fg_bg: Live compact colour-role captions beside colour values.
context.save_export: Export result does not mark the full drawing saved; all three warnings retain full drawing, still-unsaved changes, full image copy and save-before-replacement safeguard.

entries.source: %1$s exported. Your full drawing still has unsaved changes; save a full image copy before replacing it.
entries.candidate: An fitar da %1$s. Cikakken zanenka har yanzu yana da canje-canjen da ba a ajiye ba; ajiye kwafin cikakken hoto kafin maye gurbinsa.
entries.final_wording: An fitar da %1$s. Cikakken zanenka har yanzu yana da canje-canjen da ba a ajiye ba; ajiye kwafin cikakken hoto kafin maye gurbinsa.
entries.reason: An fitar da marks export, distinct from ajiye (save). Cikakken zanenka retains the whole drawing; har yanzu and ba a ajiye ba retain still-unsaved changes. The imperative requires a full-image copy before replacement, not after it.
Ajiye is the save imperative; a matsayin introduces the format/name without converting Save to Export. The numbered string argument is unchanged.
Save action and format construction are grammatical and consistent with ui_save_as; JPEG and the continuation ellipsis remain unchanged.

Gaba is a compact front/foreground caption. Beside a colour value and paired with Baya it is meaningful, not an unexplained English acronym.
Baya is a compact back/background caption paired with Gaba; the live colour-caption context resolves the ordinary positional word.

entries.candidate: Launin gaba %1$s, launin baya %2$s. %3$s allon launuka.
entries.final_wording: Launin gaba %1$s, launin baya %2$s. %3$s allon launuka.
entries.reason: Launin gaba/baya correctly name the two colours. With the catalogue expand/collapse action reading, Hausa imperative precedes allon launuka: Buɗe allon launuka / Rufe allon launuka. A leading localized action is grammatically sound.

entries.candidate: Yanayin matse ko raba yatsu da matsar da abin dubawa
entries.final_wording: Yanayin matse ko raba yatsu da matsar da abin dubawa
entries.reason: Yanayin introduces the mode; matse ko raba yatsu describes pinch/spread, and matsar da abin dubawa targets the viewed region rather than painting or transforming pixels.

Babba denotes big/main/principal and is acceptable as a standalone generic Main heading. No specific implicit palette noun or screen destination is asserted. It is an elliptical label, not an inflected modifier joined to a supplied feminine noun.

entries.candidate: E bupụrụ %1$s. Ihe osise gị dum ka nwere mgbanwe echekwabeghị; chekwaa nnomi onyonyo zuru ezu tupu ịdochie ya.
entries.final_wording: E bupụrụ %1$s. Ihe osise gị dum ka nwere mgbanwe echekwabeghị; chekwaa nnomi onyonyo zuru ezu tupu ịdochie ya.
entries.reason: E bupụrụ reports export, whereas chekwaa commands save. Ihe osise gị dum retains the whole drawing; ka and echekwabeghị retain changes still not saved. The copy is a complete image and tupu ịdochie ya puts saving before replacement. The compressed relative description of mgbanwe is intelligible.
Chekwaa is a save imperative, not export; dịka supplies the as relation before the unchanged argument. Retain the established catalogue spelling.

Ihu names front/foreground concisely; paired with Azụ and a colour value, it functions as a colour-role caption.
Azụ names back/background concisely; pairing and colour value distinguish this from a navigation Back command.

entries.candidate: Agba ihu %1$s, agba azụ %2$s. %3$s bọọdụ agba.
entries.final_wording: Agba ihu %1$s, agba azụ %2$s. %3$s bọọdụ agba.
entries.reason: Agba ihu/azụ correctly label the colour roles. An imperative precedes its object: Gbasaa bọọdụ agba / Sụkọọ bọọdụ agba are grammatical expand/collapse constructions. All arguments retain their roles.

entries.candidate: Ọnọdụ ịsụkọta ma ọ bụ ịgbasa mkpịsị aka na ịdọkpụ nlele
entries.final_wording: Ọnọdụ ịsụkọta ma ọ bụ ịgbasa mkpịsị aka na ịdọkpụ nlele
entries.reason: Ọnọdụ with coordinated infinitives correctly names a mode. Bringing fingers together/spreading them gives the gesture; ịdọkpụ nlele describes dragging the view, not editing the drawing.
Isi denotes head/main/principal and is acceptable as an elliptical generic Main heading. It needs no assumed palette section, screen destination or action.

entries.final_wording: %1$s ebimisami. Dessin na yo mobimba ezali naino na mbongwana oyo ebombami te; bombá kɔpi ya elilingi mobimba liboso ya kotya elilingi mosusu na esika na yango.
entries.reason: Ebimisami reports output/export and is distinct from bomba/bombá (save). Dessin na yo mobimba preserves the whole drawing, naino the continuing state, and ebombami te the unsaved changes. A complete-image copy must be saved liboso ya replacement. The retained French dessin loan is consistent with the stated catalogue convention.
Bomba is the save imperative; lokola introduces as. The unchanged argument can name a format; the wording does not label saving as export.

Liboso is the concise front/foreground caption. The paired colour indicator makes the role clear rather than suggesting a Next action.
Nsima is the paired back/background caption; suitable next to a colour value and contrasted with Liboso.

entries.candidate: Langi ya liboso %1$s, langi ya nsima %2$s. %3$s etanda ya balangi.
entries.final_wording: Langi ya liboso %1$s, langi ya nsima %2$s. %3$s etanda ya balangi.
entries.reason: Langi ya liboso/nsima correctly identify foreground/background colours. With the existing expand/collapse context, an imperative can precede etanda ya balangi: Fungolá etanda ya balangi / Kangá etanda ya balangi. This is action-object order, not a palette-name adjective construction.

entries.candidate: Mode ya kopusanisa misapi mpe kotambwisa komona
entries.final_wording: Mode ya kopusanisa misapi mpe kobongola eteni ya elilingi oyo ezali komonana
entries.reason: Correct kotambwisa komona: komona means seeing/to see, not a concrete viewport. The replacement describes changing which part of the image is visible, retaining finger-pinching and view navigation without suggesting pixel transformation. It is intentionally descriptive; fit has not been tested.

Ya liboso can mean foremost/principal as well as first. It is acceptable as a generic Main/primary heading, not only as a palette label; the ya construction distinguishes it from bare Liboso as the foreground caption. No particular consumer or noun referent is certified.

validation.review_basis: Direct assessment of target text, not acceptance of supplied backtranslations. Catalogue context used for Main and palette action grammar.

references.use: English catalogue: Main followed by Drawing and Color; separately, Expand colour palette / Collapse colour palette support palette action context.
Resolved actual lexical ambiguity: komona is seeing/to see, not a viewport noun.
Lexical range of (ya) liboso includes first/foremost; no inference of a specific palette section.
Additional lexical check for Main ambiguity: records ya libosó as principal (Dbnary/Wiktionary attribution). Supports retaining the generic label without inventing a palette consumer.
